title: Forsyth County advocates remind abuse victims not to be discouraged about reporting crimes - NewsBreak
text:
By Dolan Reynolds ,
1 hours ago FORSYTH COUNTY, N.C. (WGHP) — Forsyth County community advocates say cases involving sexual assault or domestic violence where investigators find discrepancies can lead to doubt from the public and discourage victims from coming forward.
The Bridges to Hope Family Justice Center of Forsyth County has assisted countless people who have endured trauma.
Forsyth County advocates remind abuse victims not to be discouraged about reporting crimes (WGHP) While Director DeWanna Hamlin says she’s dealt with many heartbreaking cases, on Wednesday, Forsyth County District Attorney Jim O’Neill shared his concerns about a woman’s claim that she was assaulted at Tanglewood Park on June 30.
“It hurts real victims that have to muster up the strength and the courage to come forward and to talk about what has occurred to them, especially as it relates to a sexual assault. That takes a tremendous courage, and what these fraudulent allegations have done is they have they will have a chilling effect on real victims,” O’Neill said.
Hamlin says that for victims dealing with any type of assault, trauma lingers.
“People remember things differently than how it happened. We also have to remember that domestic violence and sexual assault are traumatic. We know that trauma lives in the body. We know that trauma changes the brain and how people recount their experiences,” Hamlin said.
She added that it’s rare for cases to be fabricated.
“It’s important to believe people who are survivors of interpersonal violence because statistics tells us one in three women and one in four men in their lifetime will experience some sort of interpersonal violence,” Hamlin said.
Now Hamlin is reminding victims not to be discouraged from coming forward.
“If something has happened to you or someone that you love, … reach out to a family justice center, a victims service provider agency, to law enforcement, to any helping agency so they can get you connected to someone who are the experts and advocating for them and navigating resources,” Hamlin said.
